---
title: "Audit 11: which oncogene variants count as activating"
author: "Jannik Franken"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
---

## Purpose

Oncogenes count as altered with a DepMap "likely driver" variant (D19): a
variant flagged as Hotspot, LikelyLoF, HessDriver, OncogeneHighImpact or
TumorSuppressorHighImpact. Two problems showed up in audit/09:

- the flags miss canonical activating variants, such as the EGFR exon 19
  deletion E746_A750del (PC9, NCIH1650);
- LikelyLoF and OncogeneHighImpact also mark *truncating* variants
  (frameshift, stop gained) in oncogenes. A truncated oncogene is not
  activated, so these lines should not count as altered.

This notebook lists all oncogene variants in the lines used in models with
their annotations, and compares the current rule with an annotation-based
alternative.

**Decision supported:** the definition of "altered" for oncogenes (revision of
D19).

## Inputs

- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds`, `04_depmap_models.tsv`
- `data/raw/cancer-cell-lines/depmap_24Q4/OmicsSomaticMutations.csv`, `README.txt` (local only)
- `config.yml`: `contrast$oncogenes`

## Methods

According to the DepMap 24Q4 README, "A variant is considered a hot spot if
it's present in one of the following: Hess et al. 2019 paper, OncoKB hotspot,
COSMIC mutation significance tier 1." Each variant also carries its ClinVar
significance (`VepClinSig`, from the Ensembl Variant Effect Predictor).

Proposed rule for oncogenes: a variant is **activating** if it does not
truncate the protein (no frameshift, stop gained, start lost or splice-site
variant) and it is either a hotspot or classified as pathogenic or likely
pathogenic in ClinVar. Both sources are curated, so no variant is classified
by hand.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/use_case.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/plotting.R"))
config <- load_config()
raw_dir <- uc_dir(config, "raw")
derived_dir <- uc_dir(config, "derived")

data <- readRDS(file.path(derived_dir, "shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds"))
lines <- data$lines %>% filter(in_models) %>% select(line, tissue, ModelID)
oncogenes <- config$contrast$oncogenes
```

## 1. Oncogene variants and their annotations

```{r variants}
flag_columns <- c("Hotspot", "LikelyLoF", "HessDriver", "OncogeneHighImpact", "TumorSuppressorHighImpact")
variants <- data.table::fread(
    file.path(raw_dir, config$depmap$dir, "OmicsSomaticMutations.csv"),
    select = c("ModelID", "HugoSymbol", "ProteinChange", "VariantInfo", "VepClinSig", flag_columns)
) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    filter(HugoSymbol %in% oncogenes) %>%
    inner_join(lines, by = "ModelID") %>%
    mutate(
        truncating = grepl("frameshift|stop_gained|start_lost|splice_acceptor|splice_donor", VariantInfo),
        clinvar_pathogenic = grepl("(^|&)(pathogenic|likely_pathogenic|pathogenic/likely_pathogenic)(&|$)", VepClinSig),
        # current rule (D19): any DepMap driver flag
        current = Hotspot | LikelyLoF | HessDriver | OncogeneHighImpact | TumorSuppressorHighImpact,
        # proposed rule: not truncating, and hotspot or ClinVar (likely) pathogenic
        proposed = !truncating & (Hotspot | clinvar_pathogenic)
    ) %>%
    select(gene = HugoSymbol, line, tissue, ProteinChange, VariantInfo, VepClinSig, Hotspot,
           truncating, clinvar_pathogenic, current, proposed)

count(variants, gene, current, proposed)

variants %>%
    filter(current != proposed) %>%
    arrange(gene, line) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Variants classified differently by the two rules")
preview_table(arrange(variants, gene, desc(proposed)), caption = "All oncogene variants")
```

## 2. Altered lines per oncogene

```{r lines}
# a line is altered if any of its variants in the gene counts
per_line <- variants %>%
    group_by(gene, line, tissue) %>%
    summarise(current = any(current), proposed = any(proposed), .groups = "drop")

per_line %>%
    group_by(gene) %>%
    summarise(gained = paste(line[proposed & !current], collapse = ", "),
              lost = paste(line[current & !proposed], collapse = ", "),
              current = sum(current), proposed = sum(proposed),
              .groups = "drop")
```

```{r lines-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
p <- per_line %>%
    group_by(gene) %>%
    summarise(current = sum(current), proposed = sum(proposed), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_longer(c(current, proposed), names_to = "rule", values_to = "lines") %>%
    ggplot(aes(lines, gene, fill = rule)) +
    geom_col(position = "dodge") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = uc_palette(c("current", "proposed"))) +
    labs(x = "Altered lines (lines used in models)", y = NULL, fill = "Rule",
         title = "Oncogene status under the current and the proposed rule") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "oncogene_rules", uc_dir(config, "output", "audit_11_oncogene_variants"), height = 3.5)
p
```

## Interpretation

- **The two rules disagree on 10 variants in 9 lines.**
  - **Newly counted variants:** the EGFR exon 19 deletions in PC9 and
    NCIH1650, BRAF G464V in MDAMB231 and PIK3CA D549N in HCT15 (both ClinVar
    pathogenic; HCT15 already counted through another PIK3CA variant).
  - **Dropped variants:** truncating variants that the current rule counted
    through LikelyLoF or OncogeneHighImpact: BRAF and EGFR in KM12, EGFR in
    MOLT4, NRAS in NCIH1048 and a PIK3CA splice-site variant in CORL23.
  - IGROV1 keeps its PIK3CA status through another variant; its stop-lost
    variant counts under neither rule.
- **Per gene the numbers hardly change:** BRAF 13 → 13, EGFR 5 → 5 (but
  different lines), KRAS 42, NFE2L2 6, NRAS 11 → 10, PIK3CA 16 → 15. The
  proposed rule changes *which* lines count, which matters for small groups
  such as EGFR in lung (2 → 4 lines).

**Recommendation:** use the proposed rule for oncogenes: not truncating, and
hotspot or ClinVar (likely) pathogenic. It rests only on curated
annotations already in DepMap, no variant is classified by hand, and it
removes the contradiction of counting truncated oncogenes as activated.

sessionInfo()
